definitions.explanation: A rhythmic pattern in Japanese poetry where lines alternate between five and seven morae (syllable units). This meter forms the foundation of traditional Japanese verse forms including tanka and haiku.

examples.japanese: {俳句|はいく}は{五七調|ごしっちょう}に{基|もと}づいている。
examples.english: Haiku is based on the five-seven meter.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}のリズムには{五七調|ごしっちょう}が{自然|しぜん}に{感|かん}じられる。
examples.english: The five-seven rhythm feels natural in the Japanese language.

examples.japanese: {万葉集|まんようしゅう}の{歌|うた}の{多|おお}くは{五七調|ごしっちょう}で{詠|よ}まれており、{日本|にほん}{文学|ぶんがく}の{基本的|きほんてき}なリズムとなっている。
examples.english: Many poems in the Man'yoshu are composed in five-seven meter, which has become a fundamental rhythm of Japanese literature.

notes:
A compound of {五|ご} (five), {七|しち} (seven), and {調|ちょう} (rhythm, meter). The five-seven pattern is deeply embedded in Japanese prosody. It appears not only in classical poetry but also in modern slogans, proverbs, and song lyrics.

POETIC FORMS USING THIS METER:
- {俳句|はいく}: 5-7-5 morae
- {短歌|たんか}: 5-7-5-7-7 morae
- {川柳|せんりゅう}: 5-7-5 morae (humorous)
- {都々逸|どどいつ}: 7-7-7-5 morae (popular song form)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {五七調|ごしっちょう}のリズム: five-seven rhythm
- {五七調|ごしっちょう}で{詠|よ}む: to compose in five-seven meter
- {五七調|ごしっちょう}に{乗|の}せる: to set to five-seven meter

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {七五調|しちごちょう}: seven-five meter — the reverse pattern, starting with seven morae; has a more flowing, prose-like feel
- {韻律|いんりつ}: meter, prosody — the general concept of rhythmic patterns in verse
- {定型|ていけい}: fixed form — the concept of standardized poetic structures
